runners_data.name: Take The Free
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a win over 20f on Good ground on the CV; Ed Bolger-trained, 67 days off, but strong sim-going record (4/4) and a recent win suggests fitness is live — sits just off Mr Dibbs and is a genuine threat if the pace is modest.

runners_data.name: Crossing The Bar
runners_data.note: Returns from a 523-day absence for Cian Collins, which is a massive unknown; going is listed as UNKNOWN with a headgear flag, and while flat form shows ability, jumping fitness after such a layoff is deeply uncertain.

runners_data.name: Mickey Cohen
runners_data.note: Prominent type with a solid sim-going record (3/3) for Noel Meade; won over 18f on Good ground and has placed at 24f, so the 2m6f trip is a step up — handles the conditions but the extra distance is the key query.

runners_data.name: Luck Between Us
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who has placed twice at this 2m6f trip on Good ground, giving him the strongest distance profile in the field at this exact configuration; 23 days since last run and a 5lb claimer on board, but the trip form is a genuine asset.

runners_data.name: Jupiter Du Gite
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse who has placed twice from five runs on Good ground and arrives fresh on 20 days' rest; the Strand Scorecard marks him as a danger and his 2m2f-2m7f history shows versatility, though he has not won from a hold-up position on this surface.

runners_data.name: Better Times
runners_data.note: Genuine deep hold-up type by profile; his map position nearer midfield reflects a crowded rear-of-field, and his STYLE_FIT of 0.92 signals he may race slightly out of his comfort zone — his one win came on Soft ground and recent form has been modest.

runners_data.name: Mr Dibbs
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who will set the gallop unchallenged in a 14-runner field; has won over 2m2f Good ground and has experience on this course, but is 6lb out of the handicap and his form figures (0P-186) show inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Strange Currency
runners_data.note: A deep hold-up runner by nature placed in midfield by the map due to the volume of closers; STYLE_FIT 0.94 suggests he is most likely to race somewhere in the middle of the pack, but his sim-going record is poor (0 wins, 0 places from 6 on Good) and recent form is uninspiring.

runners_data.name: Arcland
runners_data.note: Strand Scorecard's top selection at medium confidence; a hold-up horse who won over 2m on Good for Gavin Cromwell and placed over 2m2f — his two wins and three places from eight similar-going runs underpin the confidence, though he is 10 years old and 15 days off a run, with a tongue-tie flag noted.

runners_data.name: Ehteyat
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner in the field at OR 121 with a 7lb claimer on board; prominent style but recent form shows a pulled-up last time and very poor sim-going figures (0W, 2P from 13), suggesting the handicap mark has him covered and the trip is shorter than his best.

runners_data.name: Free Flow
runners_data.note: Hold-up type placed in midfield due to the glut of closers; STYLE_FIT of 0.93 and a form string showing no wins or places from 5 runs on Good ground make him a difficult pick — only 7 days since last run raises a freshness concern too.

runners_data.name: In The Minus
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with two wins in his career on Good ground, most recently over 2m5f — the trip looks right and he is only a 4-year-old with scope; 23 days off, moderate sim-going figures (2W from 11), but a course-proven profile is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Pilgrims Walk
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse repositioned nearer midfield on the map; his two recent placed efforts at 2m6f and 3m on Good ground are directly relevant and his STYLE_FIT of 0.91 suggests he may travel closer than usual — the Strand Scorecard lists him as a danger, and the trip is proven.

runners_data.name: Needs Must
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's runner has been off 178 days and represents a significant fitness question; the trainer's 14-day record (4/33) is active, and his one win came on Soft — prominent style with a promising profile for a 5-year-old, but the absence and a 7lb claimer make him a speculative runner.

races.paceDynamic: Mr Dibbs is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 14-horse field over 2m6f on Good to Yielding ground at Ballinrobe, and with no obvious rival willing to pressurise him, he is set to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset. The prominent types — Take The Free, Mickey Cohen, Ehteyat and Needs Must — will likely sit just behind him, forming a compact chasing pack that keeps the tempo honest but not brutal. With Mr Dibbs able to dictate without being harried, the pace will be genuine enough over this trip to bring hold-up horses into play late, but not so ferocious as to guarantee a staying-test meltdown — the shape favours well-positioned horses who can travel into contention from mid-division rather than deep closers. Better Times, Strange Currency, Free Flow and Pilgrims Walk are all natural hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map because the field contains more genuine rear-of-the-field runners than can realistically settle there; of these, Pilgrims Walk and Better Times are the most likely to find a workable position closer to the pace than their natural style suggests.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Midfield Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Dibbs sets a measured, uncontested gallop and horses positioned just off the pace travel smoothly into contention from the third-last.
scenarios.body: Mr Dibbs' uncontested lead produces a steady rhythm that rewards horses who conserve energy in mid-division and pounce on the approach to the last two flights; this 2m6f trip on easy ground amplifies that pattern.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Dibbs' field-setting tempo is even more modest than expected and the hold-up brigade fail to quicken on the Good to Yielding surface.
scenarios.body: A slow-run race sees the prominent-positioned horses — Take The Free and Mickey Cohen — travel in comfort throughout before quickening past a weakening Mr Dibbs approaching the last; hold-up horses are caught flat-footed and lack the sprint to bridge the gap.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Honest Gallop Tests Stamina
scenarios.trigger: If the 14-runner field creates enough traffic and jostling that pace rises from the start, turning this into a genuine stamina test over the 2m6f trip.
scenarios.body: A truly run race on yielding ground exposes those who are not genuine stayers and hands the race to proven distance performers who stay every yard; hold-up horses with strong finishing profiles can get competitive if they avoid traffic.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Market Leaders Disappoint, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the principals underperform due to trip, ground or race traffic and a lightly-handicapped or fresh horse finds a gap at a crucial stage.
scenarios.body: Crossing The Bar's long absence creates complete uncertainty but its form profile and fresh conditions could see it land a blow at a big price; Needs Must, lightly raced for Gordon Elliott, could also capitalise if fitness holds.

watchPoints.text: Mr Dibbs' exact gallop pace is the fulcrum of this race — if he slows significantly in the back straight, the prominent horses Take The Free and Mickey Cohen could smother him before the hold-up horses are able to produce a challenge.

Arcland is 10 years old and has shown a tendency for modest sim-going finishes (only 2 wins from 8 similar ground runs) — if he fails to quicken from his hold-up position approaching the second-last, the Strand Scorecard confidence may look misplaced.

Crossing The Bar returns from 523 days off with genuine ability but total uncertainty over jumping fitness — watch for any jumping errors early that could compromise his race or put other runners under pressure.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Better Times, Strange Currency, Free Flow, Pilgrims Walk) means the back straight could see significant movement as true closers try to find their natural position — traffic and interference between the 9th and 11th flights is a realistic risk in a 14-runner field.

Ehteyat carries the highest OR (121) but has a 7lb claimer and very poor sim-going record — if he underperforms early and loses his position, the pace map changes as one prominent horse drops out, compressing the field behind Mr Dibbs.

runners_data.name: St Anthonys Corner

runners_data.name: Run For The Border
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer whose last two runs include a win (1st, 2m2f Good) and a second — but the redistribution to midfield means her natural closing style is compromised; the STYLE_FIT tag at 0.91 weighs on her chance in this particular race shape.

runners_data.name: You Make Me Smile
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard's top selection, yet the STYLE_FIT flag at 0.93 and redistribution from rear to midfield reflect the honest tension in her position — her best form comes from hold-up angles (nine places from 12 sim-going runs) and she is unlikely to access that gear mapped in mid-division; P A Fahy keeps the booking, which is a positive.

runners_data.name: Bossy Bird
runners_data.note: Consistent enough at OR 102 with a place at 2m4f on Good, but no win from four sim-going starts and a hold-up style that leaves her reliant on a fast-finishing shape this race is unlikely to serve up.

runners_data.name: She'll Be Kept
runners_data.note: Back-to-back winner (2m4f Soft, 2m2f Good) for Brian McMahon, and the step up to 2m6f is the principal question; hold-up style means she needs the prominent group to tire, which is plausible if Cobra Queen sets a genuine pace.

races.paceDynamic: Cobra Queen is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no obvious rival intent on disputing the lead, she should settle into a sustainable rhythm on Good to Yielding ground over 2m6f at Ballinrobe — a trip and surface that rewards horses who travel well rather than those who must make up ground late. Theflyingbee and Camlin Park are genuine prominent types who will press into the early positions behind Cobra Queen, creating a sensible but not punishing pace that keeps the field largely strung out. You Make Me Smile and Run For The Border are true hold-up performers whose natural position at the rear is unavailable given the volume of hold-up types in this field, so both are mapped to midfield — but this displacement matters, as it means neither can truly utilise their closing style. This race shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield horses who can track the leader efficiently and pick off a tiring pack in the final climb, with patient hold-up horses squeezed out of their ideal role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cobra Queen Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Cobra Queen settles uncontested in front and posts a measured gallop that never fully tests the chasing pack.
scenarios.body: Cobra Queen dictates every yard on Good to Yielding ground, and with no rival seriously pressuring, she can conserve enough energy to repel challengers from the last hurdle home; her prominent style, solid recent form at this trip and sim-going record of 6 from 6 make her the most natural beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Collar Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Cobra Queen's pace proves just generous enough for Theflyingbee and Sound Judgement to travel in comfort before asserting from two out.
scenarios.body: Theflyingbee's consistent record of placing on Good ground at 2m2f-plus gives her a sound platform, while Sound Judgement's course-proven win at 2m4f on Good suggests she relishes this type of stamina test; both sit handy enough to pounce without needing to make dramatic ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Emerges Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to flatten the prominent runners and a midfield tracker produces a sustained run from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Walkingmayotomilan won over 2m6f on Good and can travel well in midfield before delivering a sustained gallop; She'll Be Kept, a back-to-back winner, has the class to pick off tired rivals if energy is spent up front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops into a genuinely attritional test and the field is sufficiently strung out to allow displaced hold-up types to find their rhythm from the rear.
scenarios.body: You Make Me Smile and Run For The Border are both high-STYLE_FIT horses racing out of their natural position, meaning this scenario is discounted — their chances depend on conditions that this race shape is unlikely to create; even if the pace rises, neither is optimally placed to exploit it.

watchPoints.text: Cobra Queen — if she secures the front and meets no pressure through the early stages, the uncontested lead on Good to Yielding at 2m6f becomes a significant race-shaping advantage that all other horses must overcome.

You Make Me Smile — the Strand Scorecard's top selection is a low-confidence call precisely because her true hold-up style is displaced to midfield; watch whether Sean Cleary-Farrell (7) can engineer a position that at least partially replicates her natural rear-to-finish role.

Run For The Border — similarly squeezed from her natural position at the back, Peter Smithers (5) will need to make a tactical decision early; if she drops back naturally rather than settling in midfield, her STYLE_FIT concern eases but she may give too much ground in a 2m6f hurdle.

Walkingmayotomilan — the only runner in the field with a recent win at exactly this trip on similar ground; the apprentice rider is the main doubt, but the form angle is the most literal match to today's conditions and deserves monitoring in-running.

St Anthonys Corner — 345 days off and a 'fades in finish' flag make her a significant risk to race confidence; if she exits or capitulates early, the effective field of 10 reshapes midfield positioning for horses around her.

runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a strong sim-going record (1W1P from 2 runs) and a recent win at 25f on soft, making the Good To Yielding and 2m7f combination squarely in his wheelhouse; top weight at 168lbs and a 7lb claimer (Conor Smithers) require monitoring.

runners_data.note: Midfield runner whose recent win (PPP1U9) at 22f on Good came only 11 days ago — trainer Lanigan has a live 1/3 in the 14-day window; the 5-year-old is lightly experienced over fences but the sharp turnaround could mean fitness is peak.

runners_data.name: Ladies Well
runners_data.note: Strong Strand Scorecard top-rated selection with a remarkable 8/8 sim-going record including 2 wins and 4 places; recent form (-2U121) is excellent, trainer Slattery is firing (7/30 in 14 days), and the 2m7f trip on today's surface looks made for this hold-up 6-year-old.

runners_data.name: Hit The Frame

runners_data.name: The Little Yank
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse mapped to midfield given the surfeit of closers — ran only 4 days ago (P-3370 recent form) and the 11-year-old's sim-going record (0W2P from 7) at 25-26f suggests modest expectations; the quick turnaround is also a fitness query.

runners_data.name: U Asking Me
runners_data.note: Fades in the finish and carries the redistributed flag — a true hold-up type operating from mid-field in a shape that is unlikely to maximise his chance; the 0W0P sim-going record across five runs and persistent fading pattern make this a difficult case regardless of scenario.

races.paceDynamic: Kilashee is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of 19 over 2m7f on Good To Yielding ground at Ballinrobe, and with no rival willing to genuinely press him from the outset, he should control tempo from the front — though his "fades in finish" flag means that control is likely to unravel in the straight. Fr Gilligansvoyge, Las Brisas Boy, Hit The Frame and Reve Inoui are natural prominent types who will track close to the pace and are well-placed to capitalise when Kilashee weakens; Ladies Well, Mistyburn and Il Silenzio are the primary hold-up threats who will need to pick their way through a big field late. This field holds substantially more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — The Little Yank, U Asking Me, Swing Time and Set The Tone are genuine closers but are effectively pushed into midfield by the density of that profile, meaning they are unlikely to operate from their optimal position. The race shape therefore favours prominent racers who can settle just off a single uncontested front-runner and pounce when he ties up, making that stalking P-style profile the clearest tactical beneficiary.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Kilashee sets a manageable solo gallop and fades in the final mile, allowing prominent trackers to sweep past.
scenarios.body: Fr Gilligansvoyge and Las Brisas Boy travel smoothly just off the pace and inherit the lead when Kilashee weakens, with the soft-galloping Good To Yielding ground rewarding those who conserved energy in the first half. This shape perfectly suits horses that race prominently in a truly run staying chase, and Fr Gilligansvoyge's consistent placing form (3W7P in 12 runs) over similar ground makes him the archetype.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough through the middle sections to string out the field and create a genuine test of stamina.
scenarios.body: Ladies Well, with an exceptional 8/8 record on similar going and a course-friendly profile, is ideally suited to picking through a tiring field in the straight, with Mistyburn and Il Silenzio offering similar late-running threats. The Good To Yielding surface and 2m7f trip play to the stamina and jumping accuracy of horses who can get into a rhythm out the back, and Ladies Well's recent winning form (-2U121) marks her as the standout in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely uncontested and Kilashee dictates at a surprisingly even tempo that blunts the closers.
scenarios.body: Despite his fade flag, Kilashee could capitalise on a clear lead by conserving enough energy to hold on for a place, while Fr Gilligansvoyge — sitting just behind and travelling well — could arrive too late if the winning margin is forged in the first circuit. This scenario is limited by Kilashee's well-documented tendency to weaken and his modest recent form (067-PP), making a clean-lead victory possible but unlikely in a field of this size.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos In Big Field
scenarios.trigger: If the large 19-runner field causes crowding, fallers or interference that scrambles the expected race shape.
scenarios.body: With 19 runners over fences on Good To Yielding, the risks of early trouble, a loose horse or a pile-up at a fence are non-trivial, and a horse ridden prominently with a clear passage — such as Not So Serious, who won recently (PPP1U9) and runs fresh — could find daylight that others don't. Set The Tone, though mapped to midfield as a redistributed hold-up type, has genuine form placing in similar conditions and could benefit from a disrupted scenario that creates gaps.

watchPoints.text: Kilashee leads unchallenged but is flagged as a fader — watch how quickly he weakens at the third-last fence, as that moment will determine whether Fr Gilligansvoyge or Ladies Well has time to get to him.

With 19 runners over fences on Good To Yielding, watch for congestion and potential interference at early fences — any horse that loses its position or gets crowded in the first mile will likely be out of contention given the stamina demands of 2m7f.

Ladies Well carries the Strand Scorecard top rating but is a hold-up type in a race where true closers are overcrowded at the rear — watch whether jockey Alan O'Sullivan can find a clear passage through the field in the straight without getting blocked.

Fr Gilligansvoyge is 13 years old and ran 14 days ago — watch for any signs of fatigue in the closing stages; his prominent style is ideal for today but age and recency could see him flatten out after the last.

Zolpharine's trip extension to 2m7f is unproven (13th last time over 26f) despite a good record over shorter — watch whether he stays the trip or fades from a prominent position in the straight as an indicator of future potential.

runners_data.note: Won last time out over 2m (16f) in Good ground 14 days ago and handles similar conditions well (5/5 sim-going); sits just off the pace naturally and could benefit if the front-runners burn each other out, though this is a step up in field size.

runners_data.name: Le Diablo
runners_data.note: The Scorecard's top selection despite a hold-up style that suits the contested pace scenario well; 5-year-old with strong recent form (T14: 2/14) and Good-ground competence across 10 runs, though jumping from the back in a 19-runner field is the key navigational risk.

runners_data.name: Phoenix Arizona
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with four placed efforts from nine similar-going starts; no win since OR dropped, and this competitive field with strong early pace tests whether the 7-year-old can sustain his challenge from the front group.

runners_data.name: Claude
runners_data.note: One of the three confirmed leaders and carries cheekpieces and tongue-tie; apprentice jockey Peter Smithers (claim 2) will need to manage his mount's exuberance in a three-way battle for the lead, and his record shows only one placed finish from seven similar-ground runs.

runners_data.name: Stoneyford Lady
runners_data.note: A key Scorecard danger from De Bromhead's in-form yard (T14: 4/26); travels prominently, handles this ground (7/8 sim-going, 1W4P), and the tongue-tie and cheekpieces combination suggests connections are pressing for a result at 45 days fresh.

runners_data.name: Roccabaker

runners_data.name: Sayitfirst
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has placed twice at this level in Good ground and stays well enough for 2m1f; 10-year-old's age is a flag but showed 2nd finishes recently and a truly-run race through the legs of exhausted leaders is exactly what this type needs.

runners_data.name: Political Stance
runners_data.note: No jockey listed which is itself a concern; limited recent data (2 sim-going runs, 0W0P) and the form string shows only one placed finish (2nd from 3 runs), making meaningful assessment difficult in a wide-open competitive field.

runners_data.name: Bossing It
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile in Good ground with a solid placed run (2/17f/GOO) in recent history; the 6-year-old has not yet won but the hold-up style suits the anticipated pace scenario and a clear run from 2-out could bring the placed form to a head.

runners_data.name: Ballybrittas
runners_data.note: Won last time out (3rd, 1st, 3rd from last three over suitable trips in Good ground) and the midfield style means the contested pace could set up the finish well; Rothwell's yard has one winner from 26 runs in 14 days so trainer momentum is modest.

runners_data.name: Mo Ghille Mar
runners_data.note: The most recent winner in the field (1/18f/GOO) and a confirmed front-runner with headgear (hood); Hanlon's 5-year-old has the best record from the three leaders (2W2P from 11 sim-going runs) but faces a contested lead battle that may cost him dearly.

runners_data.name: Lady Doyanne
runners_data.note: Second Scorecard danger from De Bromhead (T14: 4/26); prominent style with three placed efforts from seven Good-ground starts and tongue-tie in place, but has not won from seven attempts at OR 108 and a step up from 16f trips is untested territory.

runners_data.name: Fedneys Park
runners_data.note: Consistent non-performer (0W1P from 7 sim-going runs, 000 recent form) and 89 days off; De Bromhead runner with tongue-tie but the form profile does not inspire confidence in a competitive field even with stable in decent nick.

runners_data.name: Feet On The Ground
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose best recent run was 3rd at 16f in Good ground; the 8-year-old has no jockey listed and the form tailed off over longer trips, suggesting 2m1f is the right distance but traffic from the back is the persistent risk.

runners_data.name: Poppycon
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has placed over 2m (three times at 20f in Good ground) and carries cheekpieces and tongue-tie; fell (F) in recent form and the jumping reliability question mark is significant in this competitive 19-runner chase.

runners_data.name: Coole Vision
runners_data.note: OR 75 is the lowest in the field and the only two similar-going runs produced 10th and 14th; no jockey listed and very hard to make a case for involvement at the business end of a hotly-contested 19-runner handicap chase.

runners_data.name: Itsalonglongroad
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish which is a serious concern in a stamina-testing race with a strong gallop; the 12-year-old's prominent style means it will likely be close enough early but the fade warning aligns poorly with what this race will demand late.

races.paceDynamic: Mo Ghille Mar, Leave In Secret, and Claude are all confirmed front-runners in a 19-runner field, guaranteeing a strong gallop from the outset over 2m1f on Good to Yielding ground at Ballinrobe — there will be no dawdling. Eight of the 19 runners want prominent positions, meaning the early stages will see serious congestion and jostling, with traffic problems almost certain between the second-last and last as the field compresses under pressure. The honest pace set by three genuine leaders will burn off lesser-stamina types and make this a proper test of jumping and staying power in the closing stages. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with proven stamina and the ability to pick their way through traffic from 2-3 out, as the leaders are likely to have taken each other on and left the race open for closers finishing with purpose.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Mo Ghille Mar, Leave In Secret, and Claude fight for supremacy early, setting a strong gallop that burns through the field.
scenarios.body: The three front-runners push each other along at a genuine pace across the 2m1f trip, leaving them vulnerable to hold-up horses who have conserved energy off the bridle; the Good to Yielding ground rewards stamina over raw speed at the finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent-running types secures a clean position just off the pace and stays out of early trouble.
scenarios.body: A horse like Stoneyford Lady or Farrokh settles beautifully in the top three or four without expending energy in the early scramble, then picks up fluently from the last fence with the pace run out of the leaders; De Bromhead's yard is in strong form (T14: 4/26) and prominent types who avoid congestion are rewarded.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner — most likely Mo Ghille Mar — gets a soft lead or the others tire leaving a lone pacesetter to dominate.
scenarios.body: Mo Ghille Mar has winning form at this trip in Good ground (1/18f/GOO) and Hanlon's runner showed excellent recent fitness (LR:14d), meaning if Claude or Leave In Secret capitulate early, the winner could be long gone; this scenario is tempered by the near-certainty of strong company pressing throughout.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Rally Through Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If heavy early traffic causes incidents 2-3 out and the race falls apart, leaving a fresh hold-up horse to come from furthest back.
scenarios.body: With 8 horses fighting for prominent positions in a 19-runner field, the mid-race congestion risk is real and a horse like Bossing It or Feet On The Ground could emerge from the carnage late; this is a lower-probability shape because true late finishers in big-field chases at Ballinrobe on honest ground rarely get a clean enough passage.

watchPoints.text: Mo Ghille Mar, Leave In Secret, and Claude will meet head-on from the off — watch for one of these to capitulate dramatically on the final circuit as the three-way battle extracts a heavy toll in Good to Yielding ground.

Traffic between the 3rd-last and 2nd-last is a near-certainty with 8 runners chasing prominent positions in a 19-runner field — Le Diablo, Sayitfirst, and Bossing It are all hold-up horses who must find gaps at exactly that point.

Poppycon has a fall (F) in recent form in a race where crowding and tired rivals at fences late on are likely — watch for jumping errors from the prominent group as stamina gives way approaching the last two fences.

Lady Doyanne is stepping up from repeated 16f runs to 2m1f for De Bromhead — watch whether she travels fluently through the early congestion, as a prominent racer in a scrappy race who has never proven the extra stamina is a risk even for in-form stables.

Custers Mistake (401 days absent, unknown style) and Political Stance and Feet On The Ground (no jockey listed) should be monitored in the pre-race declarations — market moves on any of these late would carry meaningful information given the data gaps.
